sn54.6:1.4: Ariṭṭha is castigated at length for his wrong views at MN 22.
sn54.6:1.7: While this claim, if true, indicates good progress, it is still partial: desire for past and future is abandoned (but not hate); hate in the present is abandoned (but not desire); and delusion is not mentioned. | Compare a similar construction at SN 21.10:3.6.
sn54.6:1.8: BJT has the verb in present tense. I follow the MS reading, assuming the future tense is further evidence of his partial understanding.
